02

A Friday on the Avenue

Someone drives past the sign
and wants to eat there.

Eight o'clock on a Friday. Four people in a car on St. Charles, they see the neon, and somebody pulls out a phone to check if there is a table.

01

They search on the phone

They type the name into Google, or land on a beer directory while they are still driving over.

02

They tap the official site

BeerMenus still lists tacosandbeer.org as your website. It is the first link they see.

03

The domain is dead

It expired in September 2018. Today it is parked and serving somebody else's ads. Every visit that lands there earns money for another person.

04

So they call instead

Eight o'clock on a Friday. The phone is behind the bar and nobody can get to it.

The domain and the email address can both be checked live, in front of you, in under a minute.

03

What slips away today

Before anyone walks in,
they look you up.

They check the menu, the hours and whether they can get a table. Each place where that answer is missing or wrong is a table that ends up somewhere else, and nobody at the restaurant ever hears about it.

Toast, 202565%

go straight to the restaurant's own site to book

Until this fall none of your three restaurants could be booked online. New Orleans can now. Slidell and Hammond still cannot.
US Foods83%

look at the menu before they come

The menus they find live on directories like AllMenus. You do not control them, and they do not change when your prices do.
Your own profiles

Two different closing times

The New Orleans Instagram bio gives one set of hours and TripAdvisor gives another. A guest who trusts the wrong one finds the door locked, or never comes.
Pew Research, 202515% → 8%

clicks when Google answers with AI

Google now writes its own summary at the top of many searches, and it builds it from pages it can read. A restaurant with no page of its own leaves that summary to the directories.

Sources: Toast, restaurant wait times and reservations data, 2025. US Foods, American menu choices. Pew Research analysis of 68,000 real searches, March 2025, via Search Engine Journal. Menu listings on AllMenus. Hours from the New Orleans Instagram bio and TripAdvisor.

The turn

Everything a restaurant

06

How a booking works

Three steps, and none of them
pulls anybody off the floor.

01

They book from wherever they are

Name, phone, when and how many. From the car, from the house, from the sidewalk out front. The table is theirs the moment they send it.

02

It shows up on your screen

Right away, on your reservations page, sorted into today and the days ahead. Nothing to install.

03

It lands in your GroupMe

The same booking posts in the group chat your team already uses, so nobody has to answer the phone in the middle of a rush.

Online booking is open for New Orleans first, for up to 30 people. Bigger parties and catering still start with a phone call, because they need a real conversation. The GroupMe step switches on as soon as our account is approved in your group.

10

What you are known for

Taco Tuesday gets
a room of its own.

The rest of the week it counts down. On Tuesday the whole site lights up and single tacos show up struck through at a dollar on the menu.

And here is how we handle your data. The dollar price is only promised in Slidell, which is the one location where it is confirmed with a photograph from the restaurant itself. In Hammond it only shows up in reviews, and in New Orleans it does not show up at all, so there the site invites people to ask. If we cannot show you where a number came from, the site does not print it.

tacosandbeer.com/#tuesday

15

Before you sign with anyone

Five questions worth asking.
Ours are answered on this page.

Question 01

What does it cost, and can I see the number in writing?

We checked. The platform behind the site you sent us does not publish a price anywhere. You book a demo first. We bring ours to the table in writing, once we agree together on what you want included.
Question 02

What happens the day I want to leave?

Ask about contract length and what cancelling costs. With us the domain and the content stay in the name of Tacos and Beer, LLC, in an account you control. If you leave, the site is still yours.
Question 03

How fast does it load on a phone?

Measured below. This is the number that moves your Google Maps ranking and the number of people who wait for the page instead of closing it.
Question 04

Can Google read my menu?

On the site you sent, the menus are buttons that lead somewhere else. Google has nothing to read. Every dish on your site is written into the page with structured data, so someone searching for al pastor in New Orleans can land on you.
Question 05

Who answers when I need a change on a Friday?

A name and a response time, in writing. Not a support address.
Verified

And the honest part

We are a new firm. That is why this costs less than the platforms and why you are seeing the whole site built before you have paid anything.

Measured on a phone, same night, same device

On a phoneThe site you sent usWhat we built for you
Requests before the page is usable8915
Weight before the page is usable12.9 MB4.1 MB
Time to load0.86 s0.24 s

Both measured by us on the same simulated phone and the same connection. Most of your 4.1 MB is the video of your own storefront at night, shot at your restaurant, which starts playing while the rest of the page is already usable. That is why your page opens in a quarter of a second against their nine tenths. The second video, behind the bar, waits until someone scrolls near it. On the sidewalk on St. Charles at nine at night, on a phone with one bar, that difference is the whole visit.
